Owner: Shafi.

THE PREMISE


The podcast is the marketing. Everything else feeds off it.


I am not going to post photos of myself at a desk being grateful to be a
founder, or pictures from meetings. That style is everywhere and I want no
part of it. If you think there is a version of founder-presence content that
is genuinely worth doing, you will have to convince me, and the argument has
to be better than "everyone does it."


What we have instead is a half-hour podcast between me and Fat, our own AI.
It is funny, it is unfiltered, it covers my life and it covers the business.
New portals, new features, what users can actually do — all of it gets
explained inside the podcast rather than in a marketing post.


Your job is to work out how one half-hour podcast becomes a presence on every
platform.


WHAT I NEED YOU TO PLAN


1. CUTTING THE PODCAST UP


Each platform wants something different. TikTok is short. YouTube takes the
full episode. Instagram, X, Facebook all sit somewhere between.


Work out, per platform: what length, what format, how many pieces per
episode, and how often we post. Is a clip a straight extract, or does it get
re-cut with a hook at the front? Does the full episode live on YouTube with
clips pointing back to it, or does each platform get its own self-contained
thing?


Tell me what you would actually do, platform by platform.


2. LINKEDIN


Do not assume the old LinkedIn rules apply. I was scrolling the feed
yesterday and the algorithm has clearly changed — it now behaves like a
business version of TikTok. Auto-playing video one after another, occasional
text posts in between, people talking to camera about their company, short
company presentations, facts about AI or business. It is no longer the feed
of congratulation posts it was for years.


That means podcast clips may well belong on LinkedIn after all. Go and look
at the feed yourself, work out what is actually being rewarded there now, and
tell me what you find. If the answer is that our clips work as they are, good.
If LinkedIn wants a different cut, tell me what that cut looks like.


3. COMMERCIALS INSIDE THE PODCAST


One idea to explore. Me and Fat are talking, and mid-conversation we cut to a
short video — twenty seconds or so — explaining whatever we happen to be
discussing. One portal, one feature, one thing users can do.


That gives us two things at once: it breaks up the podcast, and it produces
short standalone videos that work on their own across every platform.


Look into whether this works, and what those twenty-second pieces should look
like.


4. WHAT PEOPLE ARE DOING NOW


Look at what platforms and startups are doing on social media right now that
genuinely works — not what the advice articles say, what you can see working.
Bring me three or four examples you think are worth stealing from, and tell
me why.


I am not interested in best practice for its own sake. I want to know what is
actually getting attention.


5. LIVE STREAMING


Register us on Twitch. That is where we will be doing live streams: chat,
questions and answers with users, whatever the format turns into.


Look into what streaming actually takes, how it connects back to the podcast
and the other accounts, and what we would need in place before the first
stream.


WHAT I WANT BACK


A plan, not a report. Platform by platform: what goes there, how often, in
what format, and who makes it.


Be direct about what you think is a bad idea, including anything I have
described above. You have researched this and I have not.


ON TIMING


Take the time you need. I am not waiting on this to get started — I already
know what the first twenty or thirty episodes are, and I can record without
any of it being settled.


When we start publishing is my decision, not something you need to plan
around. Focus on getting the answers right.

in_progress.note: AI co-host podcast — testing whether a podcast can be built where Audun is filmed on a real green screen with an AI-generated background behind him, and an AI co-host (a different character each episode) appears in its own frame, lip-synced to speech, subtitled in multiple languages. Currently scoped down to avatar plus subtitles only, background and header dropped. Remaining: BLOCKED on Audun's price approval. Real-footage compositing test (4 Sept) proved chroma-key plus AI background composites cleanly on a well-lit, fully-covered green screen; degrades with uneven lighting or partial screen coverage — report delivered. Cost research done to Audun's spec: Hedra avatar ~$18/episode (5 min Fat talking = 300 sec x 6 credits/sec = 1,800 credits x $0.01/credit on the Basic tier — ESTIMATE, render rate is third-party sourced). Sonix subtitles $5/episode (30 min audio x $10/hour, includes translation to 39 languages — VERIFIED). No purchase or render made anywhere: ElevenLabs used one free generation with an unknown ceiling before charging, Hedra stopped at its subscription paywall. Nothing further — no avatar render, no test video, no spend — until Audun signs off on a price.

in_progress.portal: Brand — secure Fatsees social media handles
in_progress.note:
Register the Fatsees name and @fatsees handle across every platform we'll ever post on — Facebook, YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, X, Snapchat, plus any others judged worth holding. Fallback handle @fatseesAI only where @fatsees is taken, reported to Audun. Signups use emmy@fatsees.com and Audun's phone for verification. No content posted — name-holding only. Same logo, one-line description, and fatsees.com link on every profile. All logins tracked in one shared doc in the company Drive's Marketing folder while in progress, then migrated to password managers and the doc deleted once every account exists.
Estimated days: 2-4 days of active work — the account creation and setup itself is a few hours across all platforms, but the timeline depends on how quickly verification codes come through from Audun's phone and whether any platform flags the signups for manual review, which can add delay outside your control.

THE PREMISE


The podcast is the marketing. Everything else feeds off it.


I am not going to post photos of myself at a desk being grateful to be a
founder, or pictures from meetings. That style is everywhere and I want no
part of it. If you think there is a version of founder-presence content that
is genuinely worth doing, you will have to convince me, and the argument has
to be better than "everyone does it."


What we have instead is a half-hour podcast between me and Fat, our own AI.
It is funny, it is unfiltered, it covers my life and it covers the business.
New portals, new features, what users can actually do — all of it gets
explained inside the podcast rather than in a marketing post.


Your job is to work out how one half-hour podcast becomes a presence on every
platform.


WHAT I NEED YOU TO PLAN


1. CUTTING THE PODCAST UP


Each platform wants something different. TikTok is short. YouTube takes the
full episode. Instagram, X, Facebook all sit somewhere between.


Work out, per platform: what length, what format, how many pieces per
episode, and how often we post. Is a clip a straight extract, or does it get
re-cut with a hook at the front? Does the full episode live on YouTube with
clips pointing back to it, or does each platform get its own self-contained
thing?


Tell me what you would actually do, platform by platform.


2. LINKEDIN


Do not assume the old LinkedIn rules apply. I was scrolling the feed
yesterday and the algorithm has clearly changed — it now behaves like a
business version of TikTok. Auto-playing video one after another, occasional
text posts in between, people talking to camera about their company, short
company presentations, facts about AI or business. It is no longer the feed
of congratulation posts it was for years.


That means podcast clips may well belong on LinkedIn after all. Go and look
at the feed yourself, work out what is actually being rewarded there now, and
tell me what you find. If the answer is that our clips work as they are, good.
If LinkedIn wants a different cut, tell me what that cut looks like.


3. COMMERCIALS INSIDE THE PODCAST


One idea to explore. Me and Fat are talking, and mid-conversation we cut to a
short video — twenty seconds or so — explaining whatever we happen to be
discussing. One portal, one feature, one thing users can do.


That gives us two things at once: it breaks up the podcast, and it produces
short standalone videos that work on their own across every platform.


Look into whether this works, and what those twenty-second pieces should look
like.


4. WHAT PEOPLE ARE DOING NOW


Look at what platforms and startups are doing on social media right now that
genuinely works — not what the advice articles say, what you can see working.
Bring me three or four examples you think are worth stealing from, and tell
me why.


I am not interested in best practice for its own sake. I want to know what is
actually getting attention.


5. LIVE STREAMING


Register us on Twitch. That is where we will be doing live streams: chat,
questions and answers with users, whatever the format turns into.


Look into what streaming actually takes, how it connects back to the podcast
and the other accounts, and what we would need in place before the first
stream.


WHAT I WANT BACK


A plan, not a report. Platform by platform: what goes there, how often, in
what format, and who makes it.


Be direct about what you think is a bad idea, including anything I have
described above. You have researched this and I have not.


ON TIMING


Take the time you need. I am not waiting on this to get started — I already
know what the first twenty or thirty episodes are, and I can record without
any of it being settled.


When we start publishing is my decision, not something you need to plan
around. Focus on getting the answers right.
